answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, each identity locks its own refundable smart-contract bond, making multiple identities costly. A single slash occurs when cryptographic proof reveals conflicting commitments signed for the same task, creating a ripple effect that exposes malicious behavior. This mechanism helps prevent attacks from reaching their nadir, where they become irreversible. Like a glacier, this approach slowly builds resilience, protecting the system from coordinated attacks and ensuring the integrity of the network.
